rationale.selected_because: The objective has shifted from arranging a quote and inspection to reviewing a completed-work report and an invoice. The provider reported completing the work, and the invoice reports £174 of remedial works. However, the earlier instruction expressly prohibited work until a quote was reviewed and written authority issued; the provider later said he thought he had been instructed to do the work. Register the supplied invoice and related work evidence, obtain the provider’s account of the instruction/access and a cost breakdown, seek the landlord’s retrospective spend decision only after human review, and move the case to completion review—not closure.

uncertainties: The work completion is reported by the provider and described by the invoice; it is not independently verified. The source does not establish how access was arranged, who authorized work to start, or whether all invoiced items were within the original scope.

The general landlord approval did not state a price limit, while the separate instruction required quote review and written authority before work. The amount and authorization basis for this completed work therefore need review.
